commits.message:
fix(renderer): a hung renderer is ended and restarted, and a start's subscriptions and pins hold (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.v58)

Answers the medium review:

- The supervisor asks the live renderer on a timer whether its loop turns,
  over a ping its event loop answers outside its turns; one that left the
  last ask unanswered is said and ended, and the restart follows.
- A start's subscriptions go to the collector, as every turn's do.
- A dead renderer's watches and holds are released only once a start
  succeeds, never on one that failed.
- A start pins and warns every session it carries even when its view did
  not open, so the host's pinned feed is pinned in the renderer too.
- A feed whose frame step keeps throwing the same fault says it once and
  says its recovery, so a renderer's restart is not a line per frame.
- The renderer drops the host's heap cap and inspector flags, and the heap
  cap has one formula.
- A channel launch hears a last line that has no newline.
- The renderer's launcher is built before anything can launch, as the
  faults read both launchers.
- World states hold the latest update fact any document carried, so a
  document handed in late cannot move the dismiss gate back.

fix(renderer): the supervisor starts its renderer as the daemon arms and paces restarts by backoff (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.v58)

Answers the high review of the renderer's process split:

- The supervisor is a state machine (idle, live, down, closed). It starts
  the renderer on arm, off the first request's path, and restarts one that
  ended after an exponential backoff while renderers in a row end young.
  An input meanwhile fails with how the last one ended and spawns nothing;
  pins and teardown steps are carried by the next start. The launcher's
  renderer rate limit is gone: the supervisor owns the pacing.
- Pins and unpins are recorded as they arrive, so one that lands while a
  renderer is dying is not lost.
- A host call's failure keeps its kind across the wire, and the renderer's
  click dispatch classifies by failureOf rather than instanceof.
- A call reach runs as its line arrives, in order with the notices after it.
- A renderer refuses a host of another build (the boot carries the digest).
- The renderer's stderr is logged line by line, not captured for its life;
  the channel's line splitter scans each chunk once.
- The renderer launcher's lifeline faults are logged and reach the world.
- A renderer that does not end on stdin close is signalled after a grace,
  so the teardown cannot hang on it.
- A renderer start opens each session on its own.
- The renderer flushes its session state on every exit path.
- Each process is judged against the whole published limit: a fixed split
  put the host under a node baseline at a lowered limit.
- An in-process renderer loads its storage as the daemon is built.
- hosted() moves to the test helpers; dropped law markers are restored.

feat(renderer): the renderer runs in its own process, supervised and restarted by the host (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.v58)

The daemon's renderer is the bundle started again as its `renderer`
subcommand, talking one JSON value per line over its stdio. The host's
supervisor starts it on the first input and again on the next input after
it ends. Each start carries every live session with its pin, so a restarted
renderer answers as the last did.

Every id a renderer mints carries its generation. The host scopes each
renderer's watches and storage holds, releases a dead one's once the next
has started, and refuses an effect-done of an ended generation. The
renderer ends with its stdin, has its own launcher aborted last in the
teardown, and runs its own backstop over its share of the memory limit.
The update dismiss gate follows the published fact in the renderer. A
test's worker and the site page run the renderer in process over the same
interface.

refactor(renderer): a build's storage folders cross as holds, and session reads are keyed by folder (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.2r6) (#755)

* refactor(renderer): a build's storage folders cross as holds, and session reads are keyed by folder (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.2r6)

The last in-process reach, the storage owner, leaves the adapter, so every
entry the renderer reaches in the host crosses a process and the crossing
check covers all of it.

A build names its storage folders; it keys and watches none. The render cache
tells the host's storage owner which folders each served state's latest load
names (`storage.hold`), at every load, built, kept or failed, and releases
them when the state is reclaimed. So a folder's watch lives as long as a build
names it, never as long as a view or a session, and every config load is a
lost or faulted folder's recovery, as before. A reload holds its successor
before it releases its predecessor, so a folder both name stays open.

The generation is the owner's own fact: session reads are keyed by folder, a
lane carries across a generation and is re-read when it moves, and the owner
makes only the storage folder, never its plugin's folder.

* refactor(renderer): a folder's watch is the one record of its generation, and a file at its path is a fault (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.2r6)

High review of #755. The Folder record repeated what the folder's current
watch holds (the identity it opened on, whether its generation ended), so it
goes: the next generation follows the watch it replaces, the second stat on
open goes with it, and nothing outlives a folder's last hold. The storage
folder is looked at before it is made, so a file at its path, or a read-only
volume refusing an existing folder, is judged truly. A served state enters the
map before its folders are held, so a throw cannot strand it; the host alone
keys each folder once.

* fix(renderer): storage generations are numbered across folders, so a folder held again never reuses a closed watch's key (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.2r6)

* fix(renderer): a storage folder another writer makes first is no fault, and the design inventory names holds, not keys (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.2r6)
